publications.title: Merger Times and Genealogies in a Finite Gaussian Sticky-Particle Gas
publications.summary: Four sticky particles can share the same collision times and form different groups. The paper gives the conditional weights of complete merger histories in a finite Gaussian chain and bounds the probability of a prescribed sequence of mergers of labelled cores in common time windows.

readiness.next: Obtain a human specialist assessment of the proofs and their relation to prior work, then select a journal.

publications.scope: The model is a one-dimensional chain of equally spaced unit masses with independent standard Gaussian initial velocities. Both results condition on full coalescence and the first collision joining particles 1 and 2. The macroscopic bound concerns a fixed ranked planar binary tree on the cores, with the leaves in spatial order. Hitting the time windows is part of the event.
publications.verification: The preprint includes proofs of both results and an explicit four-particle calculation. Human specialist review is pending.

publications.title: A reachability threshold for random partial orders with a power-law gap kernel
publications.summary: In a directed random graph with gap-dependent edges, a density integral determines the threshold for a path between two fixed times. It also describes the limiting order seen by a sample of fixed size.

readiness.next: Obtain a human specialist assessment of the proof and its relation to prior work, then select a journal.

publications.scope: The result covers each fixed nonnegative gap exponent. It gives no uniform estimate near the threshold or as the exponent varies.
publications.verification: Mathematical proof included in the deposit. Independent human specialist review pending.

publications.title: Directed structural drift from finite relaxation in adaptive resistor networks
publications.summary: In a two-node model of an adaptive resistor network, a small voltage lag can change which node gains more conductance during long periodic training.

readiness.next: Select a journal and prepare the manuscript for its submission requirements.

publications.title: Coherent-resonant netting: disorder-enhanced selectivity from transient wave-like dynamics on biological connectomes
publications.summary: Simulations on two biological connectome benchmarks found that partial coherence can improve target-selective routing. In a fruit-fly mushroom-body motif, selectivity peaked at intermediate disorder. Rewiring the network or increasing dephasing weakened the effect.
publications.scope: The article models the routing stage with an open-system proxy. The stage that commits to a decision and its energetic cost remain outside the tested result.
publications.verification: Journal peer review. Numerical benchmarks with matched classical and rewired controls, and a permutation test for the fruit-fly contrast.

publications.title: Programming the learning-response matrix in adaptive resistor ladders
publications.summary: In a model resistor ladder, teaching can change how the network learns next while restoring its original input–output function.

publications.title: Observation-limited access to fast plasticity preparation in adaptive resistor networks
publications.summary: Even when a network can be prepared quickly in principle, noisy observations can make that ability expensive to use. The time bounds include probing and restoration.

readiness.next: Check the final submission files and make the assumptions on prior knowledge and noise explicit.

publications.title: Work-Induced Specialization and Trade-offs in Future Capabilities of Adaptive Physical Networks
publications.summary: In a specified class of adaptive conductance networks, efficient execution of a mandatory task makes some later changes faster and others slower, even when the original input–output function is restored.

readiness.next: Check the proofs and closest literature, then select a journal.

publications.scope: The theorem assumes a specified material constraint and terminal-state selection rule. It applies at a small fixed task amplitude.
publications.verification: Mathematical theorem for the stated network class. Author preprint.

publications.title: Same learning response, different preparation costs in adaptive resistor networks
publications.summary: Networks with the same present function, conductance norm and learning response can still require different amounts of time to prepare for the same local change.

readiness.next: Frame the contribution as a control problem and choose a specialist journal.
